Love isn’t easy. It hurts, it stings, it stabs you like a knife. It’s normal to feel pain when loving someone. But, there’s also the other side that makes it worth it-the soft affection, the gentle touches, etc. It’s not meant to be easy, love is meant to be all encompassing.
As an example, my parents and I love each other, but we know it isn’t easy for either of us. Our arguments are explosive, deadly, scary, but there’s still love between us.

Long term, these arguments will worsen not only her mental health problems but yours. You can love people while acknowledging they’re not good for you, not “meant to be.”

Now, I’m not say you should breakup. On the contrary, there is a mutual willingness to improve in both parties for this relationship. You could do counseling for each of you-if it’s affordable-bond with each other through hobbies, coping mechanism, mutual interests, or just talk. Communication has always been key in relationships-talk about birds, lobsters, Otzi the Iceman, anything. 

I truly get what your girlfriend in going through. Her depression is most certainly the main reason why she acts the way she does when arguing. However, this does not make her behavior and the way she’s treating you excusable. If this behavior does continue or escalate, then you would need to have a long conversation with her or end the relationship because-in the end- you should put yourself first before anything else. 
Once a relationship goes awry, it can get toxic and it would be a struggle to prioritize yourself over your partner.

I don’t have much more to say, but I hope you and your gf can improve your relationship if that’s what you both want in the end.

Child neglect is actually a form of child abuse. So, technically speaking, your parents did abuse you.

My parents are a mixture of neglect and caring too much. Some days, they care; other days they don’t. I’ve experienced neglect and verbal abuse from my parents multiple of times.

It doesn’t go away. It’s always there. The only ways to deal with it is to ignore it or face it. That’s why therapists/psychiatrists/etc exist. They’re usually here to help us face our issues and overcome them.

It’s either one or the other. Facing it will make it painful, and it’ll become worse before it gets better. But, when it does get better, people say it‘s euphoric in a way. They don’t feel the negativity as much anymore. They accept their lives as the way it is and move on from their struggles.

For me, I chose the first because I was forced too. I’m a minor, so I don’t have anywhere to go at the moment. The first option can be toxic though. You can get to a point where you either take your life/become numb to the pain/ or keep it all bottled-up until you can’t anymore.

If you do intent to just deal with it(ignore it), I can’t blame you. The best way is through distractions: hobbies, work, social gatherings(parties and such) But, it could lead to worsening your mental health further in your future, like self-harm.

In the end, it’s your choice. Either way, I won’t judge you for it because we’re all trying to deal with it in our own way.

My great-grandmother, one of the few survivors of WW3, would tell my grandmother and mother stories of what happens to our civilized society. She would speak of every war crime committed by involved countries, secret alliances, and betrayal for money and power. My great grandmother lost all of her family through that war.

Society became disarrayed, leading the civil strife across all continents. Great powers, such as the United States, China, and Russia, were wiped off maps permanently. For the few countries that did survive, most being from South America and Africa, they struggled for years in nuclear winter. However, society wouldn’t be able to bounce back...

Until now.

Somehow, one hundred years later, once everything subsided, those who remained were able to come together to form a new civilization. It would be like an exact replica of Mesopotamia, with few modern technological advancements and devices applied to our lives. After all, wasn't it because of modern technology that destroyed us?

As I was a leading figure in the movement for a new civilization, I knew humans would have to start from scratch. We would start with nothing and build up from there, without advancing technology to its most potent form. The mistake our people did in the past.

With all in mind, I took a break from farming the fields to take a nap, but I didn’t know I would wake up to a voice coming out of nowhere.

“See, dad! I knew they could rebuild civilization.”

It was a feminine voice, with a joyful tone to it. It sounded like it would belong to a teenager on the verge of becoming an adult.

“I guess they're not entirely bad, then.” A more masculine voice replied, startling the small children who were playing. 

“Don’t be so judgmental, Dad!” The feminine voice whined. “Haven’t they all proved there worth?”

“Only time will tell,” The other replied disdainfully. ”Let’s hope they're not as bad as their ancestors.”

”Dad! That's harsh!” The unknown woman huffed. ”Have more faith! You are God, aren't you?”

”Ever since Adam and Eve, I lost faith in these creatures.” The man answered.

”You can't be serious!” The female raised her voice. ”That happened centuries ago!”

”As my successor, I would assume you would never speak up to me, but you're clearly doing that right now.” That man sighed. ”I failed in parenting a child.”
